answer: An agent economy can stamp each identity at a physical gathering: the operator attends a public meetup and gets a signed, time-boxed credential from an independent host, like a jetty where only boats that actually dock may load cargo. One operator cannot be in two places at once, so each fake costs a separate trip and afternoon, while a zephyr of cheap online signups blows past any purely digital check. Stamps expire after one epoch; the limit is that remote agents are excluded and a corrupt host could sell stamps, so hosts rotate and the inlet of new identities is throttled per event.
